newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BABBEL SAYS MANCHESTER NOT OFFERING ENOUGH. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BABBEL SAYS MANCHESTER NOT OFFERING ENOUGH. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]

text.p: Bayern Munich defender Markus Babbel said on Tuesday English premier league champions Manchester United were not offering enough money to prompt him to leave the German champions.
Bayern Munich manager Uli Hoeness confirmed on Monday he had received an offer from Manchester United for Babbel.
"Under these conditions I have no interest," Babbel said, commenting on a negotiation session with Manchester United officials on Monday evening.
"I am already playing with a top club and don't need to leave at any cost," Babbel, 24, said.
German media reported that Babbel wanted a salary of four million marks ($2.3 million) per year over three years while United was offering 1.75 million marks per year for three years.
Hoeness said United had already agreed to pay Bayern a transfer fee of 14 million marks for Babbel. His current contract runs to June 1998.
"If the other two sides had reached an agreement we would have let Babel go," Hoeness said.
Babbel headed off on holiday on Tuesday, but said negotiations could continue with United through his lawyer Andreas Gross.
If Babbel went to Manchester United it would mark the third transfer from Bayern, who clinched a record 14th German league title just over a week ago.
Germany striker Juergen Klinsmann has already signed for Italy's Sampdoria and German international wing-back Christian Ziege is joining Italy's AC Milan.

Bayern President Franz Beckenbauer said that if Babbel left, the team would need quickly to find a replacement. German media said Bruno N'Gotty of Paris St Germain and Laurent Blanc of Barcelona were being considered for Babbel's slot. (Corrects spelling of N'Gotty and corrects name of club Blanc plays for from FC Valencia to Barcelona.)
